name: Audit page
description: The whole system's audit trail as a page: who changed what, when, and what the value was before. Queried across records, actors, fields and dates, grouped by day, newest first, and append-only — nothing on this screen edits anything.
when_to_use: Somebody is asking a question about the past that no record answers on its own — why a rate does not match the contract, whether an approved order was amended after it was approved, who released the QC hold in March, what a leaver touched in their last fortnight. The line against record-page and its activity variant is who is asking and where they started. record-page/activity is one record's history shown as a region of that record's page: the reader already has the record open, the trail is bounded by it, and there is no query — it is the last thing you read before deciding about that record. This is the system's trail, queried across records, actors, record types, fields and dates, and an auditor does not start from a record. They start from a question, and the filter apparatus is the component: the same event that appears as one line under a purchase order appears here beside events on four other records because they share an actor and an afternoon. Both exist and neither replaces the other — the record variant here is the same events as record-page/activity with the whole query apparatus over them, and it is what the "See the full trail" link at the foot of that region opens. Against index-page: that is a register, and the rows in a register are things — orders, vendors, receipts — which can be created, opened, edited and acted on in bulk. The rows here are events, which happened, and cannot be any of those; that is why this page has no selection, no row actions and no create, and why saying so is worth a paragraph. Against table: that is the rows and a sortable header with no page around them, and it is what a register is built from — an audit trail is not sorted by column, because the only order it has is time and it is descending. Where the question is "what does this record look like now" rather than "how did it get here", the answer is record-page.
rules: This renders inside app-shell, as the whole of <main>. The gutter is mx-auto max-w-5xl — wider than a record because an entry carries an actor, a record, a timestamp and a pair of values on one line, and narrower than a register because there is no column set to compare across.

The old value is the component. "Akshay Prabhu updated PO-2026-0418" is a receipt for an audit trail rather than one; the entry that answers the question is the one carrying ₹58,400 and ₹61,200 and the timestamp between them. Every entry that changed a field renders both values, and an entry that cannot produce the old value is a defect in what was written, not a case to design around.

Append-only has consequences on screen, and they are the unusual ones in this library. There is no selection column, no row menu, no bulk bar and no create — not disabled, absent. Every other list here grows those the moment it is real, so a reviewer will ask where they went: an event happened, and there is nothing to do to it. What the page does instead is filter, group and export, and those three are where the whole design budget goes.

Time is the only order and it is descending. The day is the unit people argue in, so the day heading is a full-bleed recessed band with one list under it — marker/grouped's shape — rather than one card per day. A card per day is what record-page/activity does because it draws at most a handful of days; a page that can draw forty of them turns into forty bordered boxes with two lines in each, and the column of marks restarts at every one.

Today and Yesterday are said in words and the date is said beside them, never instead. "Today" alone is wrong the moment the page is left open past midnight, printed, or screenshotted into a ticket, and a trail whose headings depend on when it was read is not evidence.

The timestamp is a real <time datetime> in a fixed-width gutter, so a column of times reads down the day. Relative time — "2 hours ago" — is a gloss and never the record: it is written after the absolute time, not in place of it.

A multi-field change is a grid, not a run of sentences. Field, old, new as three tracks means nine changed fields read as three columns instead of nine paragraphs, and the arrows line up down the middle. The column headings are drawn once above the band and only from sm up, because the strike-through and the arrow already say which value is which.

A value that was empty is the word "not set" and not an em dash or a blank cell, and clearing a value shows the old value struck through against the word "cleared". A blank on either side is indistinguishable from a field the export dropped.

The strike-through and the arrow are decoration. line-through is announced as deleted text by some screen readers and by most as nothing at all, so an sr-only "changed to" closes the old value. Without it the entry reads as two figures and no direction — this is record-page's rule and it is repeated here because half the entries on this page are that shape.

Colour is rationed harder here than anywhere else in the library. Most entries take the zinc-500 dot, and the palette is spent on the three that are worth stopping at: a refusal is red-600, something finished is emerald-600, and a change made after the record was approved is an amber-700 alert-triangle. Colour every entry by its verb and the column is a barcode by the twelfth row.

Nothing on this page is a live region and nothing polls. An audit trail that announces itself while somebody is reading it moves the page under the cursor, and the entry they were mid-way through is now four rows down. The reload is the refresh, and the load-more control is the only thing that adds rows.

The export is an audited event and the dialog says so before it runs. An auditor who takes a file away has done something the trail has to hold, and the scope of what they took — the count, the range, the filters in force — is exactly what the entry records. Stating it in the dialog is also the last chance to notice that the range is wrong.

The retention window is a fact of the page, not a footnote. The scope line in the header carries the earliest date the trail holds, and a query that reaches past it is a different empty state from a query that found nothing.

anatomy.description: page-header's shape unchanged: a <header> inside <main>, white over a border-zinc-200 rule, holding the breadcrumb, the one h1, the scope line and Export. No create button, because nothing on this page creates anything.
One 13px line under the h1 stating the query in figures — how many entries, between which two dates, over which record types, and that the order is newest first. It is the sentence the export copies.

index-page/filters' band unchanged: a search box, one select per axis — actor, record type, field, date range — and the chips underneath saying which ones are in force. Below sm the controls fold into a drawer and the chips never do.
One white rounded-xl panel holding every day. It has no heading of its own; the day bands inside it are the h2s.
marker/grouped's recessed band: bg-zinc-50, border-y border-zinc-100, an 11px uppercase h2, and one <ul> under it pointing back with aria-labelledby. Today and Yesterday are named and dated.

A mark, a timestamp gutter, the sentence naming the actor and the record, a meta line, and the diff band where a field changed. No hover fill, no link on the row itself — the record inside the sentence is the link.

A <dl> in a bg-zinc-50 well: field, old value struck through, new value after a decorative arrow. Three grid tracks from sm up, stacked below it, with the column headings drawn once and only where the grid is.
What an entry shows instead of a diff — the count of rows exported, the document printed, the permission that was refused, the session and the address. One line, same 12px, same well.
The count line and the pager, or the Load more control where the trail is being appended to. It is a role="status" and it is what says how much of the trail is on screen.
dialog/form's panel: the scope restated in figures, the format, and the sentence saying the export will itself be written to the trail.

behaviour: Nothing on the page mutates anything. There is no selection, no row menu, no inline edit and no delete, and no control is drawn disabled to stand in for one — the only writes this screen can cause are the export, which is itself an entry, and the filters, which are a GET.

Filters compose and the count line says what they add up to. Actor, record type, field and date range are one query; the chips are the answer to which of them is doing something, and each drops on its own because the usual cause of an empty trail is one filter set an hour ago and forgotten.

Changing a filter re-runs the query and rewrites the count line in place. The count is a role="status" that was in the document before the first keystroke, so the new figure is a change a screen reader reports rather than a block that arrives already speaking.

Load more appends the next batch under the last entry and never above it. A batch that starts on a day already on screen continues that day's list instead of drawing the heading twice, and the count line is rewritten and focused when the last batch lands, because the control that was pressed has been replaced by a sentence.
The day headings are the page's outline and they are stable. Appending never renumbers or reorders anything already drawn; the trail only ever grows downwards.
Export states its scope in figures before it runs, writes the file, and writes an entry recording who took what. The dialog is the only place on the page where a button causes a write.

At 390px the timestamp gutter moves above the sentence, the filter controls go into a drawer, and a change touching more than two fields collapses to a count with a disclosure — nine fields as twenty-seven stacked lines is an entry nobody can read past.

Deep-linking a query is the point. Every filter lives in the querystring, so the trail an auditor was looking at is a URL they can put in the finding, and Back returns to the query rather than undoing a chip.
accessibility: One <main>, one <h1> in the band naming the trail, and every day heading an h2 with the day's list pointing back at it with aria-labelledby. The heading outline is the whole navigation this page has.

The day heading is a real heading and never a list item. Written as an <li> it is announced as item 1 of 12 and every count in the group is off by one; dropped between two <li>s without one it is lifted out of the list entirely.
The timestamp is a <time datetime> carrying the full local date and time, so the 14:22 in the gutter is unambiguous to anything reading the markup rather than the heading above it.

The diff is a <dl>: the field name is the <dt> and the two values are two <dd>s under it, which is what keeps them one unit. An sr-only "changed to" closes the old value, so the pair is announced as "Rate, line 3 — fifty-eight thousand four hundred, changed to sixty-one thousand two hundred".

Every mark in the gutter is aria-hidden and every arrow in a diff is aria-hidden. The colour of a dot is a summary of a sentence that is already written out beside it; where the dot is the only thing carrying a warning, the warning is written in the entry as well.
The count line is role="status" with tabindex="-1", so it both reports a new figure and is somewhere to put focus when the control that was pressed is removed from the page.

Each chip's button is named for the filter it drops — "Remove the filter Field: rate" — because six buttons called Remove is what gets read out otherwise. Clear all is a link beside them, not a second filled button.

The export dialog is aria-modal with a focus trap, its heading names it, and the scope figures are inside the dialog rather than only on the page behind it — a dialog that says "Export?" over a scope the reader can no longer see is a confirmation of nothing.

The permission and retention empty states are prose in the region they apply to, naming the scope that is closed and the person who opens it. Not a title attribute and not a disabled control, both of which explain nothing on a phone.
